output: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter flew a routine mission in the Sea of Okhotsk, approaching and performing an aggressive maneuver towards a US RC-135U aircraft, reportedly mimicking air-to-air missile equipped behavior. This incident followed a previous encounter between a Russian jet and the US Navy destroyer Donald Cook in the Black Sea earlier in April. The escalating tensions between the US and Russia, due to Russia's involvement in Ukraine, have been an ongoing factor.

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour of Australia and New Zealand, celebrating Charles' 67th birthday with a barbecue in Western Australia, making it the 15th time Charles visits Australia, and they will meet the new Australian PM Malcolm Turnbull during their tour, which includes visits to 12 towns and cities in both countries.

A 70-year-old woman was attacking in Sneem, County Kerry, on 20 September. A man was subsequently detained by officers in Killarney on Saturday morning and is currently being questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station.

The Medical Practitioners Tribunal decided to remove Hugh McGoldrick's name from the medical register, as no appeal was filed before the 28-day deadline following a ruling against him for falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients.

A body was found in a wooded area near the Goodwyns housing estate in Dorking, and a 21-year-old male has been arrested on suspicion of murder, with Surrey Police awaiting the results of a post-mortem examination.

A man named Josh Hanson was fatally stabbed at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, around 01:10 BST on Sunday. Approximately 40 people were in the bar at the time of the attack, and Scotland Yard encourages anyone who was there after midnight or in the Field End Road area around 01:00 Sunday to share any relevant information about the incident, as no arrests have been made yet.

A proposed ferry service between Sandown and Southsea, spearheaded by local businesses aiming to boost tourism, could run provisionally on Tuesdays and Thursdays from July 14 to August 27, subject to needed permissions and pending final discussions and location agreements between the Isle of Wight Council and Hovertravel.

On Sunday at approximately 2 am BST, a 30-year-old man was attacked by roughly eight individuals in the Heights area. One suspect, also 30 years old, was arrested and later released on police bail while investigations continue; the police are appealing for information regarding the incident.

In the last two days, the death toll has doubled in flood-affected regions of India, particularly Assam, reaching over 100 fatalities and affecting nearly 450,000 people as the monsoon rains continue to affect at least 20 states. The government has provided aid packages and Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to visit Assam to find a long-term solution to the recurring flooding.

The Premier League's 25th anniversary season opens on Friday 11 August with Arsenal hosting Leicester City at 19:45 BST, with Sky Sports broadcasting the match as part of their multi-million pound deal for 10 Friday night matches. Despite this, a BBC survey has revealed that more than a third of Premier League football fans admit to regularly watching matches live online via unofficial streams.

Cristian Montano, who made 48 appearances and scored 4 goals for Oldham Athletic, was dismissed from the club following an investigation into spot-fixing by the National Crime Agency. The club, taking the matter seriously, acted swiftly in the dismissal.

Footballer Chris Wilson, aged 30, re-joined Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in August 2013, making 51 appearances over four seasons before being released in May 2018, with a history also at Preston North End and Notts County.

Vadim Cobilas, Sale's first Moldovan international in the Premiership, is leaving to join France's Top 14 team Bordeaux, with Sale boss Steve Diamond confirming negotiations for new contracts with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings. Chris Cusiter and Tommy Taylor's futures are undecided, with Wasps reportedly interested in Taylor, and Diamond is currently actively recruiting for next season.

India, led by Shikhar Dhawan's 117 and Virat Kohli's 105, were on course to record the highest successful run-chase in Australia at 277-1. However, a dramatic collapse saw them limp to 323 all out, with Kane Richardson taking 5-68, leaving Australia 4-0 up in the series, on the brink of a potential whitewash in the final match in Sydney.

The Hammersmith and City Line and parts of the Circle Line were temporarily suspended due to concerns debris from a fire in a 24-storey block could fall onto the tracks, at the request of the London Fire Brigade, with 58 presumed deaths and potential for higher losses.

Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, previously of Hearts and a former Kilmarnock youth product, has returned to Rugby Park after signing a three-year contract, set to make his 150th appearance there upon his second debut.

Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole in his ceiling while celebrating a goal scored by Paul Anderson during an Ipswich v Norwich match. Afterward, Anderson offered to pay for the repairs as a gesture of goodwill.

Retail stores in Wales are mandated to keep tobacco products out of public sight, aiming to decrease the appeal of smoking and enhance public health. Offenders might be penalized with fines of up to £5,000 and imprisonment for six months. This regulation, applicable to shops and other establishments like pubs and clubs, mirrors earlier restrictions implemented for larger stores and supermarkets in 2012.

Lucas, a 20-year-old footballer, is joining Bristol Rovers' League Two squad for a third time this season, after scoring three goals in ten appearances for a previous National League side. Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire undergoes restoration, notably waterproofing and rebuilding of the chimney stack, with night-time work on the platform canopy minimizing disruptions, as stated by Network Rail and train operator Northern; Paul Barnfield, representing Northern, emphasized Knaresborough's historical charm.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL player who served over 30 years in prison due to multiple assault convictions, is believed to have taken his own life after being placed in solitary confinement over accusations of killing his cellmate.

The article explains a proposal to extend bus lane operating hours for the Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT) plan from 7:00 to 19:00, with plans for potential adaptations based on consultation with commuters and stakeholders, and a focus on ensuring clear compliance and efficiency.

Lionel Messi scored the winning goal for Barcelona in their La Liga game against Atletico Madrid, extending his record as the competition's all-time top scorer, despite missing the game's first half due to being with his newborn son. On the same day, Real Madrid's Cristiano Ronaldo broke his club's record for league goals.

Over 70 individuals, including players and directors from Italian third and fourth division clubs, are under investigation for "conspiracy to commit sporting fraud," with links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate and involvement of some police officers. Police are investigating suspicious results in dozens of matches.

In August 1947, India and Pakistan became independent (Partition), leading to mass displacement as millions became refugees, as detailed in the CBBC documentary "Finding My Family - Partition: A Newsround special," which recounts one woman's story of her family's experience during this historic event.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner with 30 years of experience, completed 14 miles of her 20th marathon before taking the Underground to Westminster and walking the remaining distance to The Mall. She expresses joy and gratitude for the supportive crowd, especially the young people, and holds no regrets for her attempt.

In China's leading cities, some young couples have resorted to enacting fake divorces as a means to buy additional homes, due to a highly unaffordable property market that persists despite attempts by the central bank to curb rising property prices.

A 46-year-old landlord, Mr Jones, was found dead at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead. A red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van collided on the A713 near Carsphairn at about 10:40 on Friday, resulting in the deaths of both drivers, Antony Sztuka (50) and Scott Kennedy (46), both from Ayrshire. Police are seeking information from witnesses who may have seen a white flat-bed pickup truck, the size of a transit van, in the area at the time of the crash as they believe the driver may have information crucial to the investigation. The road was re-opened around 18:45 hours.

Australian rower Sarah Tait, who won an Olympic silver medal in the 2012 pairs event alongside Kate Hornsey, has been a strong role model and inspiration to many athletes. Diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, Tait continued to make a lasting impact in rowing, influential particularly with emerging female athletes.

On the day of Afghan President Ashraf Ghani's inauguration, the Taliban claimed responsibility for two suicide bombings in Kabul, resulting in injuries to military personnel and civilians, occurring in separate locations within the city, one in the west and the other in the northeast.

Daimler projects full-year sales will surpass 100bn euros, despite a slower growth in Mercedes sales in China (8%), as the company anticipates continued growth in major emerging markets, albeit at a lower rate than the previous year. Despite this, Daimler remains optimistic about future growth due to strong Q2 performance.

The 10-year-old son of Denmark's Crown Prince Frederik was rescued from a potentially fatal situation by lifeguard Nick Malcolm at Mermaid Beach. According to lifeguard Stuart Keay, the prince might not have survived without the timely rescue.

An elderly man was found deceased on Elgin Road at its junction with Inchbroom Road, and both police and firefighters responded to the fire at about 16:10 on Wednesday. Initial police inquiries suggest no suspicious circumstances, and a joint fire investigation will take place. The man's name has yet to be released, and no one else was injured.

A specialized clinic for veterans with complex amputation-related complications has opened at the Surrey-based Defense Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC), offering superior treatment. This program is managed by staff with over a decade of experience in managing rehabilitation for military casualties. It will share knowledge and best practices with the NHS and is designed to provide these veterans, who have made significant sacrifices for Britain, with superior treatment, similar to the tertiary referral system within the NHS.

Enforcement cameras on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot have caught around 125 speeding drivers daily in less than a week, fewer than the 700 daily violations during a pre-Christmas pilot. The Welsh partnership seeks to educate drivers on speed risks, prioritizing engineering solutions before enforcement.

A Manchester-born man, living in Spain, is under investigation for secretly photographing his students, distributing child pornography online, and possessing a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors. Police discovered these activities, including use of a cloud storage service, and are trying to identify the victims in his photos. He reportedly had a special obsession with a girl he taught and may have previously resided in the Seville area.

Sturgeon fish named Steve, valued at up to £1,000, swam out of a water center at Romsey, Hampshire during a flood, escaped, and was later found in a deep puddle a mile away with minor injuries but overall healthy. A similarly valued koi carp named Chadwick is still missing.

A collision occurred on the motorway between Tamnamore, resulting in the closure in both directions and causing long traffic backups. Police advise motorists bound for Belfast to exit at junction 15, while those headed towards Enniskillen in County Fermanagh should exit at junction 12 and travel via Armagh city. Anyone with information about the crash or the man's Honda Civic before the incident is asked to contact the police on the non-emergency number 101.

The French government's proposed ambassador to the Vatican, Laurent Stefanini, has not yet been approved by the Vatican, with the extended silence indicative of a potential rejection as the Vatican usually responds within six weeks and traditionally remains silent on declined nominations. Stefanini, a top French diplomat and former deputy ambassador at the Holy See, is seen as one of France's best diplomats, and his nomination coincides with the progressive stance on LGBTQ+ rights France exemplified by legalizing same-sex marriage in 2013. This nomination has been perceived as a significant test for Pope Francis, who has shown a more tolerant view towards homosexuality, as indicated by his 2013 statement, "Who am I to judge?"

The Nasdaq suffered its largest one-day drop since April 2019, plummeting 2.4%, due to sharp declines in semiconductor, biotech, and other tech stocks; this slide coincided with a 1.4% decrease in U.S. durable goods orders in February, leading to a decline in the Dow Jones (1.6%) and the S&P 500 (1.5%).

Vondrousova, the Czech 233rd-ranked player, beat Kontaveit and Strycova to advance close to the top 100, while Coric, the Croatian 20-year-old 79th-ranked player, saved five match points to win a five-set match against third-seeded Kohlschreiber, securing his first ATP title at the Grand Prix Hassan II.
Stoke City signs Cameroon international and former Germany youth player, Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, as their fourth acquisition of the summer transfer window.

A 56-year-old man named Seamus McCollum, who had cerebral palsy and lived in a private nursing home in Randalstown, died last September. The death was not initially classified as a murder but was reclassified as such in April this year after an autopsy. Following the autopsy results, a woman is currently being questioned by the police in connection to Mr. McCollum's death. The care home was located in Randalstown, Northern Ireland, not Maine in the United States.

Heavy rains have caused waterlogging on main streets in India's Tamil Nadu state, disrupting normal life, affecting at least 80,000 homes in northern Sri Lanka, necessitating evacuations, damaging infrastructure, and prompting a $75m relief fund from the state government, with the Chief Minister stating that extreme rainfall has condensed typical monsoon conditions into just a few days.

The McGill's 904 bus service experienced a fire on the A7660 Kilbirnie Road at around 13:35 on Saturday. The driver successfully evacuated all passengers, including a mother and her partially-sighted daughter, who later expressed gratitude for the driver's actions. No injuries were reported, and the road was closed temporarily before reopening. The burnt-out bus was later removed.

Jake Ball, a 25-year-old cricket bowler, has an impressive start to the 2016 County Championship season with Notts, leading Division One with six wickets in each of the first two games, partnering Stuart Broad in the bowling attack.

The article describes the unveiling of a memorial stone, crafted from Jersey granite, in the French village of Guillemont. This stone honors 120 Jersey soldiers, referred to as "the Jersey Pals," who were lost during the Battle of the Somme in World War I. A portion of the stone will be taken back to Jersey and incorporated into a monument in Royal Square.

John Boyega, who played Finn in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and was a member of Theatre Peckham's company from age nine to 14, is currently filming Star Wars Episode Eight. He expressed his honor to give back to the theater where he started, stating "As a graduate of the company, I am honored to be in a position to give back." The theatre's founder Teresa Early believes Boyega will be a tremendous inspiration for the young members, adding: "Now there's an act for them to follow."

In the ongoing European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat and Fitzpatrick are tied at the top with four birdies each, as Donald (2013), Westwood, and 16 other players trail closely, with Donald expressing hope for another strong round. Bradley Dredge had to withdraw due to a viral infection, despite being just two shots off the lead beforehand.

In the County Championship match, Middlesex has a strong position for their first win of the season, with Ashton Agar Voges (128*) and Dawid Malan (147) producing a crucial 279-run third-wicket partnership, despite losing early openers Nick Gubbins and Sam Robson. Hampshire hopes to salvage a draw, with poor weather forecasted for the third day. (Nick Gubbins and Sam Robson were the openers, Voges formerly played for Australia, not England.)

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically injured following an incident on Penilee Road on Friday. Police released an image of a 54-year-old man they wished to speak to, who has since been located in the Dumfries and Galloway area. The scene has been cordoned off and forensic officers have been carrying out investigations.

John Lennon's childhood home at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, was purchased anonymously in an auction after a "bidding war," for an estimated price between £150,000 and £250,000, and the property, containing three bedrooms and a rear yard, is known for its historical significance and proximity to Penny Lane, made famous by The Beatles, attracting interest from both national and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, has denied owning a dog that fatally attacked David Ellam (52) while out of control in public, pleaded guilty to possessing cannabis on the same day, and is scheduled for trial on February 5, with the possibility of an earlier date, following the August incident near Huddersfield, Yorkshire. Mr. Ellam died from his injuries at Huddersfield Royal Infirmary.

A 22-year-old man, Thomas Bebbington from Shrewsbury, was identified as a body found on private land near Leighton, about 10 miles away from Shrewsbury city centre, following his disappearance near the Dana Steps earlier on 10th November.

Tiny five-week-old otter pups are currently being hand-raised, requiring six daily feeds. As they mature, it is hoped they'll be moved to a large, outdoor enclosure with a pool and ultimately weaned onto live food during the summer.

A 33-year-old mother of four, Joanne Thompson, was found deceased at her home in Old Mill Court, Newtownards. Police are requesting witness accounts of any disturbance at a bonfire on Dakota Avenue on Monday, as well as any activity near her home on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning.

The Tiree officer for RSPB Scotland is hopeful about their successful breeding season in Iceland.

Rangers coach, previously first-team coach under Walter Smith and Ally McCoist, will not return for pre-season training under new manager Mark Warburton, suggesting potential alterations to the coaching staff at Ibrox.

A 15-year-old student, Asad Khan, died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School in Bradford. His family believes he was a victim of bullying, as he expressed feelings of unease at school and a belief that life was hard. The coroner is considering summoning a boy who conversed with Khan for testimony during the ongoing inquest.

The unique 17th-century painting, presumed to depict the 1654 coronation ceremony, which has been in Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle, since at least 1880, is undergoing restoration. The painting's origin, creator, and value are yet to be determined, as experts have not been able to identify either. Notably, this is the sole painted representation of the coronation.

Macclesfield Town wins against Wrexham 3-0, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker. Missed penalty by Wrexham's Jordan White. The victory places Macclesfield in seventh place, seven points from the play-off spots, while Wrexham stays in 15th position.

Spain coach Julen Lopetegui called up Diego Costa, Juan Mata, and Iker Casillas for the World Cup qualifiers against Belgium and Liechtenstein, with David de Gea, Sergio Ramos, David Silva, and others also included in the squad.

A 5-kilometer wildfire, believed to be deliberate, is currently spreading across a border, causing concern due to the risk it poses to both the countryside and local communities, with authorities urging the public to stop starting fires.

Irish cricketer Boyd Rankin, who appeared for England from 2013 to 2014 (11 times), is eligible to play again after ICC regulations allowed him to return to Ireland on 18 January 2016. He has agreed to a comeback following discussions with Cricket Ireland and will be available for matches such as the InterContinental Cup against Papua New Guinea (31 January to 3 February) and the ICC World Twenty20 in India, with hopes of helping Ireland gain Test status.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, formed in collaboration with the Patient Client Council and advocated by individuals like Jane Stewart affected by rare diseases such as Spondylo Ephysial Dysplasia, works to magnify the voices of sufferers and their carers. Its main objectives include education, the provision of special services, and support for enhanced treatment and care for those living with rare conditions across Northern Ireland. The partnership also seeks to lobby and advocate on behalf of those affected by rare diseases with no other outlet for self-expression.

Gloucester Cathedral aims to establish a girl chorister program, recruiting young, talented singers from local schools and various backgrounds, with auditions scheduled for April 23rd, and the first rehearsals set for September. The new choristers will contribute to the cathedral's musical worship, starting with Monday evensong from October, and also participate in Christmas and Easter services. This initiative, according to the dean, will ensure that girls have a continuous presence in the cathedral choir for years to come.

Chelsea winger Pedro was hospitalized after sustaining an injury during a 3-0 victory in Beijing, stayed overnight for observation, and is anticipated to wear a protective mask upon his return to training. The rest of the Chelsea squad are currently in Singapore, preparing for matches against Bayern Munich (Tuesday) and Inter Milan (July 29).

Former England cricketer James Taylor, who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, is now working with the academies of Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire, as well as doing media work. According to head coach David Ripley, Taylor's impressive 50-over average makes him an excellent source of advice for the teams' batsmen. Meanwhile, ex-Northants captain David Sales, who scored over 22,000 runs in more than 20 years, is working with Nottinghamshire's batsmen, with Ripley emphasizing Sales' cricket brain and experience as valuable assets for the squad.

A man is due in Belfast Magistrates Court on December 5 for charges including criminal damage, disorderly behavior, and assault on police, after an incident at 15:00 GMT on Friday afternoon on Whiterock Road, which was reportedly witnessed by people picking up prescriptions, including children.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, causing a volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats, tow the yacht to Carrick Marina, and complete a joint operation of their inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

Ipswich clinched a thrilling 4-3 victory over MK Dons with goals from David McGoldrick, Brett Pitman, and Martyn Winn (not Varney), while opposing manager Karl Robinson lamented a season of mixed performances.

A motorist from Darlington is set to appear in Maidstone magistrates on 17 February, charged with dangerous driving, causing serious injury by dangerous driving, and criminal damage. On August 27, a bridge collapse on a motorway near the M26 junction between junctions four and three left a motorcyclist with broken ribs, but no fatalities. The incident closed the main route to the Channel Tunnel and Port of Dover, with two large cranes at first clearing the debris, and a re-closure necessary the following weekend to remove the remaining bridge debris.

In the Spanish town of Platja d'Aro, a large-scale prank orchestrated by several Germans, involving pretending to chase a nonexistent celebrity and behaving like paparazzi, resulted in panic turnings into a stampede, leading to injuries for 11 individuals and hospitalizations for three. The event was later found to be a false alarm, with selfie sticks mistaken for weapons causing the chaos. Police were called, but no actual weapons were found.

Jeremiah Regis, aged two-and-a-half, was found with over 100 injuries, including a chest bite, on November 20 at an address in Wolverhampton. Sindyann Regis, 25, and Chevaze Mcgregor, 27, were charged with his murder, with the court hearing that Jeremiah died of abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma. The case was adjourned until December with a provisional trial date set for 25 April. The family of the deceased boy described Jeremiah as a "lovely, quiet, innocent little boy who was always smiling."

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, Devon, has caused injuries due to smoke inhalation and burns, with 20 fire engine crews, a police helicopter, and firefighters on site to combat the blaze that has engulfed a vast area of dry heath-land. The nearby Woodbury Park Golf and Country Club has been evacuated as a precaution, and the public has been advised to avoid the area due to smoke visible for miles.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association, led by chairman Keith Chapman, has secured a future for the club with an agreement and a 15-year lease signed for the team's Beaumont Park venue. Upcoming meetings are scheduled to finalize the management structure, schedule a race night for the 2017 season, and address other arrangements.

Elizabeth Bowe, aged 50, died three days after being severely injured at her home in Bobby Jones Place, St Andrews, on September 17th. Her brother, Charles Gordon, 51, has been charged with her murder and is currently in custody, with the investigation focusing on the initial police response leading up to the incident. The Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC) are investigating and will submit a report on their findings to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service (COPFS) in due course.

Jim O'Brien, the former Celtic and Motherwell midfielder, has signed a two-year contract with Ross County on a permanent basis, returning to aid the development of younger players. His availability for the Scottish League Cup match against Hibernian is pending international clearance.

Northants reduced Durham to 126 all out in Division Two, with key batsmen like Paul Collingwood and Michael Richardson among the wickets. Although Northants lost three early wickets, Max Holden and Chesney Hughes were unbeaten on 19 and 16 respectively, leaving them 59-3, 107 runs behind.

Lydia Ko, at two over par, trails joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim by one stroke after two rounds at the Sahalee Country Club women's major, with Henderson and Lee at two under, and Catriona Matthew at one over following a three-under round. Only five players, including Americans Gerina Piller and Brittany Lincicome, are under par at the halfway stage. Ko thanks her putter for maintaining her position. Henderson is pleased despite a drop in the final hole.

Scotland manager Gordon Strachan has reappointed former footballer Steve Watson as his assistant, reuniting the duo who played together at Aberdeen in the 1970s and 1980s. The appointment follows the departure of Stuart McCall, who moved to manage Bradford City. Watson worked with Strachan under Alex McLeish during the Euro 2008 qualifying campaign, and he previously worked alongside Mark McGhee under their new role as assistant coaches in the Scotland team.
Giants defeat Belfast 5-1 with goals from Shields, Martinelli, Garside, Foster, and Saviano; Devils beat Coventry Blaze 5-3 on previous evening.

Jordan Spieth, the defending champion, suffered a sudden collapse on the final day of the Masters, with a quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th, costing him a potential victory. Englishman Danny Willett capitalized on the meltdown, becoming the first Englishman since Faldo in 1996 to win the tournament.

Inflation in food prices increased by 4.9% in June, led by rising pork prices, with the overall inflation rate remaining below the government's target. Analysts and economists foresee China maintaining a neutral monetary policy to manage implications of property bubble risk, global economic uncertainty, and reduced economic growth aim of 7.5% (slowest rate in 23 years), scheduled at the release of Q2 GDP data on July 15.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away after collapsing during training with Chinese second-tier club Beijing Enterprises on 5th June; his memorial was attended by former teammates and family, with Senegal striker Papiss Cisse stating Tiote was like a brother to him.

In the fifth stage of the race, Slovak cyclist Peter Sagan won an uphill sprint, placing second overall behind leader Nairo Quintana. Geraint Thomas, representing Team Sky, moved up to sixth overall, with two stages remaining.

Cuadrilla's plans for fracking at Preston New Road, worth around £50 million, were approved, despite a pending legal challenge, with the hopes of spending up to half of that money in Lancashire on jobs, investment, and community initiatives. The company expects to start work early next year.

Three teenage boys from north-west London, initially reported missing in March due to suspected plans to travel to Syria, were arrested in Turkey but later released without charge after police investigation. These events mirror the case of three London schoolgirls who went missing in February and are believed to have traveled to Syria and possibly joined IS.

Hospital respiratory consultant Dr Christopher Davies criticized the hospital for buying a blackout blind for £22.95 from Homebase, which was later deemed too expensive and was rejected by the hospital management, according to the hospital's statement to the BBC. NHS England is currently investigating the situation.

Adam King scored on both sides of the break in Swansea's 2-0 win over Reading. Their development squad secured the league title against Wolverhampton Wanderers in March, while the senior team narrowly avoided relegation after Crystal Palace beat Hull 4-0 in the 2016-17 season.

Following December 2013's severe storms that damaged dunes at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, there is evidence of natural re-establishment. To strengthen the defenses, the council is considering creating a secondary dune system due to the narrowness of the existing dunes being a cause for concern. This decision arises from evacuations and power losses in homes during flooding in Rhyl, Denbighshire, a severely affected area.

The FA Cup match between South Shields (Northern League Division One) and Bridlington Town (Northern Counties East League), occurring on 19 August at 12:30 BST, will be live-streamed across BBC Sport's digital platforms, allowing audiences to watch on PC, mobile, connected TV, and BBC iPlayer. Interaction with the commentary team is possible using #bbcfacup, with responses during the game. Notably, South Shields, led by Argentine former Sunderland and Middlesbrough full-back Julio Arca, previously triumphed at Wembley in the FA Vase final last season.

In Edinburgh, a 38-year-old man sustained serious but non-life threatening facial injuries in a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road on Friday night. A 49-year-old individual was uninjured. Police are urging witnesses to report any suspicious behavior or vehicles seen in the area around this time to help establish the full circumstances of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter for the death of Jonathan Baines, also known as "Willy", following his visit to pubs in Gainsborough after a day out at Market Rasen races. She was remanded in custody ahead of sentencing on 21 December.

A 15-year-old boy suffered facial injuries, including an eye injury, after being punched and stamped on by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterson station. The incident occurred during a busy service between Glasgow Central and Neilston around 23:30 on Saturday 3 October, and his mobile phone was stolen. British Transport Police are asking anyone who was on the train and has information about the attackers at Patterson station, who remained on until the train arrived at Neilston at 23:40, to contact them urgently.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April by the North East Counter Terrorism Unit, while two 17-year-olds, Hassan Munshi and Talha Asmal, are suspected of having traveled to Syria to join Islamic State in March. This has prompted an ongoing investigation by West Yorkshire Police and counter-terrorism officers. Notably, Hassan's brother, who was convicted under the Terrorism Act at the age of 16, had a guide to making napalm on his computer found by police.

The Giants' forwards Jonathan Boxill, Craig Peacock, and Colin Shields, alongside netminder Stephen Murphy, are in the 22-man GB squad for the 11-14 February tournament, fighting to progress to the final qualifying stage for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang. This includes 17 players from the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning team in the Netherlands. During the tournament, Italian Serie A side Cortina will play against the Belfast Giants for the first time, competing in the 'Olympic Series' at the SSE Arena on February 12 and 13.

Matthew Perry is taping a contribution for a tribute to the show's creator James Burrows, not a full "Friends" reunion as previously assumed. His former co-stars are expected to take part in the special, airing on NBC on 21 February. Meanwhile, Perry will star in his play The End of Longing, a dark comedy about four people approaching middle age, which runs in London's West End from 2 February to 14 May.

31-year-old Jones, who previously played for Manchester United, Preston, Derby, Blackburn, Wolves, and Oldham, made 41 league appearances for Burnley last season, helping them win the Championship title. He started the team's Premier League season with a defeat by Swansea earlier this year.

Joe Acquaro, a prominent lawyer in Melbourne's Italian community, was murdered, with investigators suspecting underworld connections due to ongoing tensions between criminal groups in Australia's second largest city. Acquaro owned a cafe and represented criminal figures accused of offenses such as extortion, drugs, and arms trafficking.

On July 15, 2017, Air France Flight 374 from Paris to Vancouver carrying 294 passengers was diverted to Prestwick Airport, Scotland, due to the appearance of a slight smell of burning on board. A second aircraft was sent to return passengers to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

A severe weather warning has been issued for coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, particularly Aberporth, Aberystwyth, and Anglesey, as Hurricane Gonzalo approaches the UK on Monday night, with anticipated winds up to 70mph in exposed coastal regions and heavy rain from Tuesday, potentially disrupting travel and increasing the risk of surface water affecting roads, while some sailings between Holyhead and Dublin have been cancelled.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding and long wait times, particularly affecting children, as demonstrated by the experiences of patients Lilly and Jake, who had to endure lengthy waits for medical attention at a children's hospital in Sheffield. The article also involves an interview with a doctor and a visit with these patients to learn about their experiences.

A 34-year-old man from Poole was charged with causing grievous bodily harm, a 57-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice, and was later bailed until July. Kenneth David Dickie, aged 64, died from serious head injuries at the Rockley Park site in Poole on Sunday 8 May, and passed away at Southampton General Hospital on Saturday.

Former Manchester United forward Macheda will be at Nottingham Forest until season's end, despite limited appearances due to loan spells at QPR, Stuttgart, Doncaster Rovers, Birmingham City, and Cardiff since his Old Trafford career. Manager Russell Slade believes Macheda requires more playing time, and the deal includes a 24-hour recall clause. Additionally, Forest midfielder David Vaughan has signed a one-year contract, while the acquisition of midfielder Andre Moritz was unsuccessful due to complications in releasing him from his Thai Premier League side, Buriram United.

The article reports that missing worker Christopher Huxtable, one of four workers who went missing following a building collapse in February, was found dead on Wednesday, with his colleagues forming a guard of honor as his body was driven off the site. Two other workers, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, are still missing. Swansea East MP Carolyn Harris expresses her sadness for the family and reminds the public of the ongoing search for the remaining two missing workers.

Bosnia-Herzegovina international is nearing full fitness after recovering from a hernia injury but his availability remains uncertain for the upcoming match against QPR. Midfielder Jordan Cousins is ruled out for the rest of the season due to a quadriceps injury, while on-loan winger Kazenga LuaLua is still a question mark due to an ankle injury. Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of winning against QPR to close the gap on Forest, Burton, and QPR in the standings.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, selected by ESA in 2009 and traveling to the International Space Station in 2013, described his spacewalk experience as "absolutely fantastic" and he was "giddy with excitement." On his mission, he completed two spacewalks, orbited Earth 2,656 times, and traveled a total of over 110 million km.

Sixteen-year-old Joe Arundel, a former England Knights player who made 44 first-team appearances for the Tigers scoring 16 tries, expressed excitement and a bit of nervousness about joining Hull FC, a large club known for fostering a winning mentality and nurturing promising young talent, according to Hull's club director of rugby, Shaun McRae.

Ulster Bank, a subsidiary of RBS, is working to update payments for over 600,000 customers affected by a recent IT issue, promising that no customers will be left out of pocket, echoing a major IT meltdown in 2012 that impacted millions of customers over several weeks. Since the 2012 incident, RBS has invested hundreds of millions of pounds to improve its computer systems.

In the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, Omari Mwanahamisi scored twice to give Tanzania a 2-0 lead over Kenya, but Kenya managed only a single response from Christine Nafula; Ethiopia won the third-place play-off match against Uganda with a score of 4-1.

McDonald's Japan experiences a potato shortage due to industrial action at West Coast U.S. ports, leading to rationed French fry portions at their 3,100 outlets. Meanwhile, butter shortages persist in supermarkets throughout the country.

The upcoming Classic Horse Race on June 3rd will feature high-profile participants including Permian (winner of Dante Stakes at York) and Khalidi, which lifts the total purse to £1.625m. The favorite is John Gosden-trained Cracksman, who previously defeated Permian in the Derby Trial. Remarkably, a 1,000-1 outsider, Diore Lia, will also race, with the owner's emphasis on securing publicity and funds for Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital.

Antoine Griezmann, the top La Liga goalscorer for Atletico Madrid, has a haematoma on his left foot. After an X-ray ruled out a bone injury, he will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast on March 6th and will begin treatment on Monday. His team, Atletico Madrid, trails league leaders Real Madrid by six points after 11 games, with the home match against Real Madrid scheduled for March 6th.

A veteran rugby league prop player, Willie Mason, who played 290 NRL games, won the 2004 Premiership with Canterbury, and has international experience, is joining Laurent Frayssinous' troubled Super League side, the Dragons, after a season at Manly. Mason played for five NRL clubs throughout his career and represented the Kangaroos in 24 tests.

A new survey indicates an 11% increase in dog waste on UK beaches, with a marked 71% rise in Scotland, posing health risks due to the presence of bacteria; the Marine Conservation Society praises increased use of bags for cleanup, urging pet owners to dispose of them in dog bins instead.

The Supreme Court ruled that the 2013 government-introduced fees for employment tribunal claims, ranging from £390 to £1,200 per case, were unlawful and indirectly discriminatory, as they prevented access to justice, particularly for women. Union leader Dave Prentis declared this a major victory for employment rights in the country.

Dagenham & Redbridge lost to Wycombe Wanderers with players from both teams receiving red cards. Wycombe moved up to sixth place, while Dagenham remain in the relegation zone. Manager John Still believes the team is improving and has the potential to win multiple games.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, successfully nested in the Low Gelt Quarry for the second consecutive year, and the chicks are expected to fledge in the next few weeks, with over 1,000 visitors drawn to the RSPB viewpoint.

A man's kayak capsized on the fast-flowing River Wey in Guildford at around 13:10 BST on Monday, leading to a search operation involving emergency services. The public is advised not to enter the water, as it is a popular kayaking spot, and a flood warning is in place. Previously, the Wey Valley Kayak Club, located nearby, had warned that the river was not safe.

A young girl in Rabat Zoo, Morocco died following an unpredictable incident in which an elephant threw a stone over a fence, injuring the girl. According to the zoo and elephant experts, such attacks are rare in captivity and may have resulted from elephant frustration or boredom. Video footage of the minutes following the incident showed the elephant picking up the stone just prior to the girl's injury.

MP for North West Durham, Ms. Glass, joins the Labour party's shadow cabinet during a wave of resignations, with her predecessor, Ms. Powell, stating that Mr. Corbyn's position as leader has become "untenable." Ms. Powell praised Mr. Corbyn's decency and kindness but expressed no confidence in his ability to provide an effective opposition, citing her opposition to his policy on academies.

Chelsea lead the English Premier League with 59 points, with a five-point gap to sixth-placed Manchester United. Six teams, including Manchester United, are considered strong title contenders. Chelsea face a difficult match against Burnley at Turf Moor, where the Clarets have won their last seven home games in all competitions, earning 28 of their 29 league points this season at home. Antonio Conte stresses the importance of focus and concentration for his team to avoid losing points in the title race, as there are teams near the bottom capable of winning and drawing games.

Police and community support officers in Llangefni have enacted a dispersal order, enabling them to remove troublemakers, safeguard residents from persistent anti-social behavior, and safeguard young people from the potential hazards of excessive alcohol consumption. Under this order, individuals under 16 can be taken home or to a secure location, while repeat offenders could be banned from the area for 24 hours or face arrest for returning.

The Netherlands international, Marten de Roon, appeared in 33 Premier League games for Middlesbrough during the 2016-2017 season, scoring five goals. Manager Garry Monk has identified Lewis Baker, a midfielder from Chelsea, as a potential target for the Championship club during the upcoming season.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, an award for humorous children's books established by Michael Rosen in 2008, will be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations, aiming to strengthen its impact and ensure a robust future for this unique and successful prize.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, a 74-year-old white supremacist, was sentenced to death for a 2014 shooting in Kansas that resulted in the deaths of William Corporon (69), Reat Griffin Underwood (14), and Terri LaManno (53), outside the Jewish Community Center and a Jewish retirement center. Despite admitting to the crimes and expressing his desire to target Jewish communities before his death, Miller remained unrepentant during his sentencing.

The city council plans to introduce a self-service bike scheme, similar to London's 'Boris bikes', in April 2017, with 500 bikes located at various easily accessed sites including district centers, universities, and strategic locations near public transport facilities, and financed through sponsorship income without costing the taxpayer. A previous, smaller trial ended in 2011.

"Senegal international Sakho, who missed the start of the season due to a back problem and subsequently underwent surgery, is currently undergoing light rehabilitation training and needs several weeks of pre-season work before he can potentially be considered for selection in the Premier League following three months of rehab."

The NI Residential Property Price Index shows a 0.8% quarterly rise in average property prices in Q3 2020, with the biggest annual increase in Antrim and Newtownabbey (7.3%) and the smallest in Ards and North Down (2.1%). Annual growth rates reveal terraced houses with the highest rise (7.1%) compared to apartments with the lowest increase (4%). The overall average standardized price is approximately £124,000, and 5,200 deals were completed in the quarter.

The article explores the challenges of transporting large wind turbine parts on country roads in Dumfries and Galloway, as shown by two recent incidents: one successful delivery at Bargrennan Bridge in November, and a more recent incident where a delivery on the A713 resulted in a lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board proposed temporary downgrading of services, including maternity care, at Glan Clwyd Hospital due to staffing shortages, but this was halted by a legal challenge. Residents are protesting against the potential closure of maternity services at Wrexham Maelor and Ysbyty Gwynedd hospitals, fearing it would force women to travel further for care. The health board has launched a website for public feedback on various proposals, including retaining all services, and several public meetings are scheduled for September to address concerns and gather input from residents.

South Africa's Mignon du Preez scored a century (116 off 99 balls) to help South Africa to 272-6, with MAS Klaas taking early wickets in Ireland's innings, resulting in Ireland being all out for 204, giving South Africa a 68-run victory in the ODI match.

British high jumper Katarina Peake, aged 30, seeks to break her own Welsh record and secure a Team GB spot for the Rio Olympics by achieving a personal best of 4.40m (already her best) at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium, which is equal to the Rio qualification standard of 4.50m, set by British Athletics.
A fire, believed to be deliberate, involving scrapped railway sleepers at a building site in Llanwern lasted over 10 hours before it was extinguished, prompting a police investigation.

A charitable event, including a Nepal-themed concert known as the Singing Bowl Concert, was held in Edinburgh, Scotland, initiated by the Nepal Scotland Association and Mercy Corps, with assistance from the city council, to raise funds for those affected by the recent devastating earthquake in Nepal, many of whom were friends and loved ones of Association members.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's coach, was automatically suspended from the touchline for a return Europa League match due to protests against a referee's decision which led to a penalty shootout loss. Hibernian has since appealed the suspension imposed by UEFA for his dismissal during a match in which a goal disallowed on offside was a key factor.

A fire started 1,100m under the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, hospitalizing seven workers and prompting an improvement notice from the Health and Safety Executive. The company has agreed to collaborate with investigators and continue to prioritize safety, involving over 1,100 employees at the one of Europe's deepest mines.

A 23-year-old British man and a French tourist were removed from the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, for a minor offense against morality; they have not been arrested or charged, with the Foreign Office communicating with the Peruvian authorities about the situation.

Ivan Rakitic, the 28-year-old Croatian international, is set to sign a new contract with a £109m buyout clause at Barcelona, after playing in their recent 6-1 Champions League win against Paris St-Germain.

A couple in Halstead experienced critical injuries during a two-hour torture ordeal at their home on 26 April. The crime, committed by three men at around 21:00 BST, involved a break-in. The perpetrators are described as one black man and two white men, with the black man estimated to be approximately 5ft 10in tall. Police continue to pursue leads in this ongoing investigation.

Event takes place at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan on 25 and 26 July, with Dizzee Rascal headlining the opening night, followed by performances by Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling. The Saturday night headliner will be announced in the coming weeks.

In the Aviva Premiership, Foden scored his third try in two matches as Northampton Saints beat Harlequins 24-3. Both Foden and Quins' Brown, who haven't played for England since 2008, aim to secure spots in the England squad for the Six Nations tournament, with Lancaster set to announce his squad on Wednesday. Brown has scored 10 tries in 17 starts for Quins to help them lead the Premiership table, while Foden is hopeful that Northampton will provide several players for the England squad in the upcoming Six Nations tournament.

A fatal motorcycle accident occurred in Dagenham on Friday, involving a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira car. The 22-year-old motorcyclist passed away, while the 10-year-old rear passenger sustained serious injuries. The 7-year-old passenger and 38-year-old driver of the car were unharmed. No arrests have been made, and the police are requesting witnesses to provide information about the incident.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, whose flagship product crisaborole, a cream for eczema, is awaiting FDA approval, as the company seeks to target a significant unmet medical need for eczema patients, who number between 18 million and 25 million in the US, where currently few safe and appropriate treatments are available. If approved, crisaborole could generate $2bn in annual sales, as per Pfizer's estimates.

On Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, at 23:00 BST on Saturday, police handled a street fight and recovered a collection of large knives, scissors, and cannabis from a crowd. Two minors, aged 17 and 15, were arrested on suspicion of possessing an offensive weapon and assaulting police, respectively. No injuries were reported during the event, and the police later commended their swift action for averting a potential tragedy.

A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens, near the Cardiff Civic Centre. The man was taken to Cardiff Bay police station.

Conservative MSP John Lamont resigned from the Ettrick, Roxburgh, and Berwickshire constituency to contest as a Westminster candidate aiming to defeat SNP's Calum Kerr in a by-election for Scotland's most marginal Westminster constituency. Meanwhile, the Liberal Democrats have nominated Catriona Bhatia as their candidate.

The EU Commission has authorized the sale of beef from the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany to Canada, a move driven by Canada's recognition of the EU's comprehensive efforts to eradicate BSE. This decision follows a challenging period for EU farmers due to a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand impacting farm exports, particularly the dairy sector. The US has similarly resumed importing EU beef, under stringent monitoring.

The European Commission plans to sanction unresponsive tax haven nations, as per the Panama Papers revelations, and negotiates a unified EU list of non-cooperative jurisdictions, with the number of inclusions yet to be determined, alongside agreements for exchanging information about company owners and a potential crackdown on banks and tax advisers facilitating offshore tax evasion.

Archaeologists discovered Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and remains of grain-drying kilns at Torvean, suggesting they may have been used to heat water for various purposes such as cooking or wool washing during the construction of the West Link in Inverness, Scotland.

Oldham Athletic secured a victory against Southend United, with Main scoring after Forte's pass, while maintaining a six-point advantage over the League One relegation zone, leaving Southend in 13th place.

Irish actor Lally, renowned for his roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and numerous Irish language films, peacefully passed away following a brief illness. He is survived by his wife Peggy and their children Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus. He also gained notoriety for his roles in the RTE soap opera Glenroe, and the BBC series Ballykissangel, and made appearances in the Hollywood film Alexander and the Oscar-nominated, animated Irish film, The Secret of Kells.

Derby City Council committed to keep Moorways Pool open for a year, after finding savings in back-office areas and management restructuring, following a petition with over 4,000 signatures against its initial plan to close the 33m pool due to its repair needs, leaving only one other public pool in the city, potentially affecting weekly teaching for 1,200 young swimmers.

Children previously held by Boko Haram are currently being detained, without proper legal process, in a military barracks in Maiduguri, a concern raised by human rights groups, following counter-insurgency operations against Boko Haram in Nigeria.

Hearts player Alexander sustained a broken cheekbone last week, while Gallacher twisted his ankle in training, potentially sidelining him for the upcoming Edinburgh derby. Coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing former Motherwell goalkeeper Lee Hollis as a potential replacement for injured Neil.

A professional basketball player, Chelsey Lee, won the Women's Korean Basketball League's (WKBL) rookie of the year award for her team, Bucheon KEB Hana Bank, but is under investigation for allegedly falsifying her and her father's birth certificates to claim South Korean heritage. The WKBL has suspended Lee's records, annulled the team's records, and is eliminating the extra quota for international players with Korean heritage due to the suspected document fraud.

Small businesses based in business parks also face challenges in getting access to broadband services of 10Mbps or more.

Paul Pogba's emoji was displayed on boards at Old Trafford following his mixed performance against Liverpool, and he later acknowledged fans' support on social media. Zlatan Ibrahimovic, who scored the equalizer, praised Pogba for handling pressure and stated his personal aim is to help Manchester United win rather than individual awards. Ibrahimovic currently tops the Premier League Golden Boot race with 14 goals, tied with Diego Costa and Alexis Sanchez.

Hamilton admitted Ferrari outperformed Mercedes in Melbourne, but expects fluctuating results throughout the season. Southwark Crown Court is hearing a trial where former celebrity manager Mr Clifford is accused of exposing himself and forcing a woman to perform a sex act, which he denies; his Police interview comprised of multiple "no comment" responses, and the trial has been adjourned until Monday for his testimony.

Ospreys coach Steve Tandy expects a physically intense match against rivals Scarlets in the Pro12, aiming to bridge the 14-point gap between them, and highlights the entertaining style of play the team has displayed in their recent European matches. This major Hindu festival is also observed by Sikhs and Jains, with a spectacular fireworks show, Rangoli street art, and stage entertainment being some of the highlights. Additional events included art and craft exhibits at Newarke Houses Museum and Gardens and several shows at Curve theatre. Various new attractions have been added to the region to cater to the growing number of visitors, including destinations from Peru to Ireland.

The Church of England and the Church of Scotland have agreed to grow together in communion and strengthen their partnership in mission, as detailed in the Columba Declaration. Both churches value their ecumenical relationships and are open to further exploration of partnership as the report is discussed and received.

A decorated soldier, Ben Parkinson, received thousands of friend requests on Facebook during his participation in the Olympic torch relay, despite Facebook limitations on friend associations due to his popularity. His mother praised the public support, which included calls, emails, and requests to visit popular places with the torch.

The largest known drug operation at Beirut airport, involving five individuals, including a reported prince, was intercepted, with over two tonnes of Captagon pills seized. Known for its widespread consumption in the Middle East, Captagon has funded conflicts, like in Syria, and contributes to Beirut airport's reputation as a major hub for global amphetamine seizures.

The Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command is investigating claims, with Kids Company, a charity led by Camila Batmanghelidjh, prioritizing the safety of its clients while maintaining robust protection policies externally reviewed regularly. The police and NSPCC are seeking relevant information from the public.

The Queen, turning 90 this week, is known for her mimicry skills, particularly the local brogue at Sandringham in Norfolk and an impressive Scottish accent from years at Balmora in Aberdeenshire. She is known for her sense of humor, as shown by her amusing stories, such as an encounter with an unrecognizing shopper at Sandringham. The Queen will celebrate her birthday at Windsor Castle.

The United Nations Agency for Human Settlements' report indicates that Latin America, the world's most urbanized region, experiences extremely high income inequality, with the richest 20% earning 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The region, at the end of an era of urban expansion, has shown reductions in poverty, indigency, and unemployment, and is positioned to transition towards a focus on quality of life, equity, and sustainability, particularly addressing the cited challenges of job deficits and labor informality.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation for sharing a Facebook post advocating the death penalty for sex offenders, initially posted by the far-right group Britain First. She also opposes the removal of English-stream education at Ysgol Llangennech, sparking controversy within her party. Plaid Cymru accuses Labour members of collaborating with UKIP to undermine the council's decision, and has called for the party to address this divisive campaigning.

The Iraq War Families Campaign Group, led by relatives of British soldiers killed in the Iraq War, launched a crowdfunding campaign after the Chilcot report's publication to seek legal action for potential unlawful actions amid the conflict. The report criticized the UK's legal basis for military action led by former PM Tony Blair, who has not apologized for the decision to go to war itself. The funds raised will help assess the potential for a legal case against key individuals involved in the Iraq invasion.

Syed's defense team is granted a chance to reopen the 1999 murder case of Hae Min Lee, due to a Baltimore judge allowing new evidence submission, including re-examining mobile phone records and a potential alibi witness' testimony, who claims to have seen Syed in a library during the suspected crime period. The Serial podcast's investigations brought fresh doubts into the case, and his first lawyer's oversight of the alibi witness' testimony is a key focus in the potential appeal.

A 16-year-old boy, who cannot be named due to legal reasons, pulled a machete on a taxi driver in Dundee last November after attending a party, prompting one of his friends to steal the driver's change. The teen, who has previously served custodial sentences for assaults committed when he was 14 and 15, will be sentenced next month after social work background reports have been prepared.

John Clancy, a five-time Labour councillor candidate, has been elected as leader of Birmingham City Council by a margin of one vote, replacing Sir Albert Bore on 1st December. His election comes amid scrutiny from a government-appointed review panel investigating potential corruption and mismanagement within the council. Clancy's plans include providing new homes, improving social housing, expanding regeneration outside the city centre, and offering free school meals for all primary school children. Some party critics question whether he has the necessary clout and vision to prevent government intervention.

The June issue of Empire magazine's interview with actor Moore detailed his discussions with Bond director Guy Hamilton about avoiding deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery, while delving into producer Barbara Broccoli's thoughts on Connery's role in redefining the traditional leading man image, as well as the contributions of "unsung hero" Yat Malmgren and Dr No scriptwriter Terence Young in shaping Connery's Bond portrayal.

Witches' marks, historically believed to offer protection from witches and evil spirits, are mysterious symbols found in many medieval structures across the UK, with examples dating from around 1550 to 1750. This Halloween, Historic England aims to document these marks, found in buildings such as residences, churches, and tithe barns, to better understand past religious beliefs and common rituals associated with them.
